_note: Hand-authored scores for INTERPRETER-DESIGN-SPACE.md (task coordinator). Scores 1-5; weights sum to 100; totals and recommendations are computed by tools/gen_coord.py, never typed.

options.name: PowerShell-faithful tiered pipeline (AST → expression trees → light interpreter → JIT)

fidelity: It is the strategy PowerShell itself uses, so observable behavior is reproduced by construction (TIERING-POLICY, EQUIVALENCE-SPEC).
sandbox: Expression trees and call sites run arbitrary delegates; hooks exist at binders and runtime helpers but the JIT tier bypasses interpreter-level checks.
startup: The interpreter tier starts cheaply but the compiler front end builds trees for every block (COMPILATION-MAP).
throughput: Hot blocks and loops are JIT-compiled after 32 calls or 16 iterations (TIERING-POLICY).
debug: Sequence points and debugger hooks are emitted in both tiers (IR-SPEC §5).
aot: Expression.Compile and Reflection.Emit need a JIT; under NativeAOT trees fall back to a slow interpreter.
determinism: Asynchronous promotion makes the executing tier nondeterministic (TIERING-POLICY §7.5).
memory: Trees, instruction arrays, call sites and caches are retained per block.
observability: ETW compile events and script block logging exist (02.5 §14).
complexity: About 6,600 lines of compiler plus the interpreter, binders and DLR dependency.

gates.note: AOT: JIT tier and Expression.Compile unavailable (EXTERNAL)

fidelity: Every protocol of IR-SPEC §5 can be implemented once in the evaluator; no PowerShell-visible behavior requires a compiled form.
sandbox: All execution passes through one evaluator, so policy checks sit at every node visit and call.
startup: No compile step: execution starts at the first node.
throughput: Each node costs a virtual dispatch and allocations for values; no slot access without a resolver pass.
debug: The evaluator is the debugger: breakpoints and stepping are plain hooks on statements.
aot: Pure managed code without dynamic code generation runs under NativeAOT.
determinism: Single tier: results never depend on promotion timing.
memory: Only the AST is retained; no trees or instruction arrays.
observability: Trace of statements and calls is trivial to emit.
complexity: Smallest implementation; the main work is the language rules, not an engine.

gates.note: Fidelity depends on implementing the protocols of IR-SPEC §5 and the equivalence obligations EQ-01..EQ-08

fidelity: A VM can implement the same protocols; the extra translation step adds risk of divergence from the AST semantics.
sandbox: A VM executes only its own instructions, so hooks go into the instruction loop.
startup: A compile step to bytecode is cheap compared with trees but not free.
throughput: A tight instruction loop beats tree-walking (PowerShell's own interpreter is of this kind, INSTRUCTION-SET).
debug: Needs source maps from instructions to sequence points.
aot: Managed bytecode interpreter has no AOT constraints.
memory: Instruction arrays and constant pools per block.
observability: Instruction-level tracing is possible but noisy.
complexity: A compiler, an instruction set and a frame model must be designed and tested.

gates.note: Must reproduce flow-control and error-action protocols in the instruction set

fidelity: PowerShell compiles to expression trees; behavior is reproduced via the same IR (COMPILATION-MAP).
sandbox: Compiled delegates run unchecked CLR code once produced; policy must be emitted into the trees.
startup: Tree building and Expression.Compile cost start-up time; PowerShell avoids it by interpreting first.
throughput: JIT-compiled delegates are the fast path of PowerShell hot code.
debug: Debug info is possible (DebugInfo nodes) but stepping compiled code is harder.
aot: Expression.Compile under NativeAOT degrades to an interpreter.
determinism: Compile on demand with caching is deterministic if synchronous.
memory: Delegates and trees are cached per block (CompiledScriptBlockData).
complexity: Needs the compiler, binders and caches but not the light interpreter.

gates.note: AOT: Expression.Compile falls back to interpretation (EXTERNAL)

fidelity: PowerShell uses Reflection.Emit only to define classes and enums (TypeDefiner), not for the dynamic language core.
sandbox: Emitted code calls the CLR directly; checks must be emitted explicitly.
startup: Emitting and loading assemblies costs the most start-up time of the options.
throughput: Emitted IL is JIT-compiled to native code.
debug: Debugging emitted code needs symbol emission.
memory: Dynamic assemblies stay loaded unless collectible (AssemblyLoadContext).
observability: Emitted code is opaque to tracing.
complexity: Emitting IL for dynamic scoping, pipelines and error-action semantics is the most complex option.

gates.note: No evidence it can host the dynamic-scoping core (INFERENCE); emitted code bypasses evaluator hooks

fidelity: It cannot run user scripts; it only compiles the shell's own built-in commands.
sandbox: Generated code is reviewed at build time and calls only allowed APIs.
startup: AOT or R2R code needs no JIT at start-up.
debug: Generated code is debuggable like normal C#.
complexity: A source generator is extra work but each command stays plain code.

gates.note: Complement for built-in commands, not a strategy for user scripts

options.name: Hybrid: tree-walker plus bytecode tier for hot paths

fidelity: Behavior is defined by the tree-walker; the bytecode tier must match it (EQUIVALENCE-SPEC applies).
sandbox: Both tiers are interpreters, so hooks are placed in two loops.
startup: Starts as a tree-walker; bytecode is generated only for hot code.
throughput: Hot paths run the bytecode loop.
debug: Two tiers need two debug paths.
aot: Managed code only; no JIT requirement.
determinism: Deterministic if promotion is synchronous and count-based.
memory: AST plus bytecode for hot blocks.
complexity: Two engines and an equivalence test harness.

gates.note: Build only after S1 is verified; triggers in INTERPRETER-DESIGN-SPACE §7
